## My Thinking

I have about 8 mu of flat land. My family has farmed this land for generations. Here in Quzhou, everyone does wheat then maize — it fits our water, our soil, our market. I do the same. I'm not going to try something new and risk a bad harvest. We need the income to be stable.

For wheat, I'll plant in October like always. I'll buy improved seeds from the county seed store — the hybrid kind is expensive and I'm not sure it's worth it for wheat here. Four waterings gets me through: before winter sets in, then at jointing, heading, and grain fill. I know the aphids come in late spring so I spray twice. I rotary-till after the maize comes out in September, then prep the beds.

For maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste, the season is short. Everyone uses hybrid seed for maize now, that's just how it is. Summer rains help so I only water twice unless it's a really dry year. Fall armyworm has been a problem these past few years so I spray at least twice.

My husband helps during busy periods but I manage the inputs and scheduling day to day. I aim to keep costs down on fertilizer but I don't want to under-fertilize and lose yield — I'll follow what my neighbor Li uses, she gets good results.
